name: James Blake
notes: "The harmony is the entry's strongest parameter" — the research says so directly — so this model's centre of gravity is the chords block: "piano-voiced extended chords (m9, maj7#11, add-tension clusters), gospel plagal cadences, chromatic inner-voice motion, and progressions built to be reharmonised on each repeat. Long pedal tones and unresolved suspensions; both major and minor tonics, often ambiguous." That is a plagal family, a pedal single-chord family, the section's highest `adjacentSecondProb`, a very low triad share and both a major and a minor cycle so the tonic stays ambiguous. The modelled kit's floor is the middle of his three states (see the kick note at the end for the third): "a very sparse electronic kit, one deep sub-kick per bar and a single reverbed snare on 3 (half-time), **with silence between hits used as a rhythmic event**" — one kick per bar at the bottom of the density band, `halftime_3`, and a hat carpet at the section floor. The low end stays an 808 because the entry says this is where the lane's 808 practice comes from — "a very deep, clean sine sub with a slow attack and long release, functioning as a harmonic pedal rather than a percussive hit" — so it is legato, low-passed, in the lowest register in the section, and barely slides. "Space as structure" is a long intro, a low fill rate and a high `switchUpProb` for "sections that arrive with no transition". ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are the swing amount, every drum number and the 808 figures; the entry is `[LOW-CONF]` on tempo and marks drum values as idiom inference. ⚠ `confidence` is medium — the research rates it medium-high. ⚠ `session.bpm.mode` is **INFERRED**: the number is not stated in the entry, and it is an authored centre of gravity inside the band the entry does state. ⚠ **`session.keys` is INFERRED.** The entry's Keys line describes the harmonic grammar but names no key centre, so these values and their weights are an authored choice — no key in this set is stated in the research. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 949/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.4 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `melody.densityPerBar` went from [1, 4] to [2, 5]. A lead allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves the counter almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter density recovers what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present rather than busier — the floor is what moved and the ceiling carries the density claim. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "acoustic and electric piano, choral vocal stacks, and heavily pitch-shifted and formant-shifted vocal samples used as instruments — his central technique. Melody is a soft, high, controlled tenor into falsetto at very low note-density, with long rests and gospel ornament; the vocal is stacked into wide choir textures and also chopped into rhythmic fragments.", and every claim in it still holds after the change. ⛔⛔ **The kick now reaches the third of the entry's three drum states, because the second one alone made this model's variety its parent's property rather than its own (2026-08-17, `base_swap.rs` swap-collapse gate).** Measured: **46 distinct beats in 200 seeds over `lofi-hiphop` against 169 over `trap-soul`** — and the whole of that difference was two coin-flips the model does not author and `trap-soul` happens to supply (`kick.andOf4EveryOtherBar` 0.5 and `snare.fullTimeVariantProb` 0.1). Restoring them by hand lifted it only to 91; what actually closes it is the research's own third state, which this model had never encoded: *"three states — (a) no drums for whole songs; (b) a very sparse electronic kit, one deep sub-kick per bar and a single reverbed snare on 3 (half-time), with silence between hits used as a rhythmic event; (c) a **UK-garage/2-step** shuffle at 130–140 with a **syncopated kick**, a skipping hat and a snapping snare."* The entry's own tempo line names that subset — *"plus a genuine 130–140 UK-garage/2-step subset `[LOW-CONF]`"* — and this model's band is 120–150 with the mode at 132, so state (c) sits inside the tempo it already generates at. `kick.densityPerBar` therefore runs [1, 3] rather than [1, 1]: the floor is still state (b)'s one deep sub-kick a bar and only the ceiling is new, so roughly a third of bars take the extra hit. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `syncopation` 0.2 is not sourced — it is a quarter of `uk-garage`'s own 0.8, that genre being the lane the entry names and one this model already lists in `relatedGenres`, and the entry marks every drum value as idiom inference. ⚠ **`andOf4EveryOtherBar` was deliberately NOT authored here**: it is a trap idiom this entry never describes, and copying a parent's parameter onto the child to buy a number back is the thing the gate is looking for.
